newsitem.title: USA: FASB draft rule would let firms hedge with options.
newsitem.headline: FASB draft rule would let firms hedge with options.

text.p: Companies would be allowed to use net written options to offset their risks under the Financial Accounting Standards Board's latest derivatives accounting rules draft, an official said Thursday.

Earlier drafts of the rules would have banned such a practice, but the board eased its stance after hearing the concerns of several organizations, said Scott Marcello, an accounting practice fellow at FASB.
"The latest decision by the board would allow net written options to be used as hedging instruments in limited circumstances," he said.
For instance, companies could offset the risks associated with issuing callable debt by using these special options.
"The company could write an option to offset the purchased call option in the debt and leave a situation which would be just as though they had issued non-callable debt," Marcello said.

Such an approach can be attractive for companies because sometimes there are opportunities for arbitrage in the market, he said. By using these options, companies can synthetically issue non-callable debt. Often it is a cheaper alternative, he said.

The board's latest move on Wednesday, follows its decision last week to press on with a final statement on the controversial hedge accounting rules, even against Congressional pressures to slow up the process.

Although certain issues remain to be resolved, the basic approach in the hedge accounting statement is to require all derivatives to be recognized in the financial statement and to be measured at fair value, the accounting board said.
Gains and losses resulting from changes in fair values would be accounted for depending on the use of the derivative.
Marcello said FASB is likely to have the rules published late next month for a 45-day comment period, after which the rules could become final by year-end.
